docs.title: WiCrackAgent
docs.text:
Automated wireless security assessment framework — GPU + CPU dual engine, live web console, and client-ready pentest reports.

pip install wicrack
wicrack serve          # → http://localhost:5000

Authorized use only

WiCrackAgent exists for penetration testing of networks you own or are contracted to assess. Unauthorized access to computer networks is a criminal offence in most jurisdictions. Read ethics before your first run.

docs.title: What makes it different
docs.text:
1. A staged, adaptive pipeline instead of a single wordlist shot. Twelve ordered stages go from cheap-and-likely (ESSID as password, best64 rules) to expensive-and-thorough (OneRuleToRuleThemAll, phrase generation), with heavy stages gated behind keyspace estimates.
  2. It learns. Stage H converts keys recovered during the engagement into structural masks and re-attacks with them — if the environment uses Word+Year passwords everywhere, WiCrackAgent finds that pattern itself.
  3. It finishes like a pentest, not a script. Every run produces a client-ready HTML report, a tamper-evident evidence file, and an encrypted results vault.

docs.title: The 60-second tour
docs.text:
wicrack selftest                     # verify tools + end-to-end crack
wicrack serve                        # web console (upload → start → report)
wicrack crack -f ./wifi_captures     # CLI pipeline
wicrack bench                        # hardware benchmark

Continue with the Quickstart, or jump straight to the Web console and CLI reference.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
capture (.cap/.pcap/.pcapng)
        │
        ▼
 ┌─────────────────┐     hc22000     ┌──────────────────┐
 │ capture/        │ ───────────────►│ capture/parser   │──► targets, filter
 │ converter       │                 └──────────────────┘
 └─────────────────┘                          │
                                              ▼
 ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 │ core/jobqueue.JobManager (worker thread, stop events)      │
 │   convert → parse → filter → potfile pre-check → pipeline  │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
            │                              ▲
            ▼                              │ snapshots
 ┌──────────────────────┐         ┌─────────────────┐
 │ stages/pipeline      │         │ web console      │
 │ 12 Stage classes ────┼──attacks─► Flask + WS     │
 │ (AttackSpec objects) │         │ REST /api/v1     │
 └──────────────────────┘         └─────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
 ┌──────────────────────────┐
 │ engines/EngineSelector   │  GPU → hashcat · CPU → john
 │ hashcat_engine / john    │  mode 22000 / wpapsk
 └──────────────────────────┘
            │
            ▼
 potfile → core/store (SQLite) → reporting/ (HTML, evidence, vault)

docs.title: Key concepts
docs.text:
• AttackSpec — a declarative attack (kind, wordlist, rules, mask, generator). Stages plan; engines execute. Adding a new backend means implementing one Engine class.
  • Stage — a strategy with attacks(ctx) and optional enabled(ctx). The pipeline orders them, applies heavy-gates, and harvests potfiles.
  • JobManager — single worker thread + queue, shared by CLI and web; every mode sees identical behaviour.
  • Store — SQLite for results/runs; the source for reports, analytics and stage H's mask learning.
  • Stop semantics — STOP terminates the current engine process and drops queued jobs; the potfile preserves whatever was already cracked, so a re-run resumes instead of repeating work.

docs.title: Web layer
docs.text: Flask application factory (create_app) with injected engine/manager — that is also how the test suite runs the whole console without hashcat. Live updates ride a WebSocket with polling fallback; the REST API is a plain blueprint documented in src/wicrack/web/static/openapi.yaml.

docs.title: Benchmarks
docs.text:
Numbers depend heavily on hardware, drivers, and OpenCL runtime. Run:

wicrack bench

and submit your result via PR (one row, include GPU/CPU model and engine).

Hardware Engine WPA speed Reporter be the first — PR your wicrack bench output!

docs.title: Reading the numbers
docs.text:
• WPA-PBKDF2 (mode 22000) is deliberately slow — 4096 HMAC-SHA1 iterations per candidate. Consumer GPUs land in the ~50–300 kH/s range; a modern laptop CPU in the ~5–30 kH/s range with John's SIMD kernels.
  • That is the security property of WPA being assessed: an 8-char random password is computationally out of reach, a Company2023! is not.
  • Use the benchmark with the stage estimators: auto_ok_hours decides when a heavy stage runs unattended, and that maths is only as good as est_speed.

docs.title: Ethics & authorization
docs.text:
Read this before your first run

Cracking a WPA key of a network you do not own — or lack written authorization for — is a criminal offence in most jurisdictions.

docs.title: The authorization checklist
docs.text:
• [ ] Written authorization (SOW / ROE) signed by the network owner
  • [ ] Scope documented: SSIDs, BSSIDs, time windows, locations
  • [ ] Data handling agreed (where captures and recovered keys live, retention)
  • [ ] Local law checked (CFAA, Computer Misuse Act, StGB §202c, IT Act, …)
  • [ ] Client informed about deauthentication side effects
  • [ ] Artifacts encrypted at rest (wicrack vault, full-disk encryption)

docs.title: Why this tool ships with reports
docs.text: A pentest without a deliverable is a hobby. WiCrackAgent generates the client-facing HTML report (executive summary, findings, remediation) and an evidence file with SHA-256-hashed keys — so the engagement output is defensible and the plaintext keys can stay redacted in shared copies.

docs.title: Responsible disclosure of results
docs.text: Every recovered key is a finding, not a trophy: rotate it, document it, help the owner move to WPA3-SAE / 802.1X. That is the entire point.

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: Machine-readable automation surface; the web console itself consumes these endpoints. Spec: src/wicrack/web/static/openapi.yaml (vendored at /static/openapi.yaml when running). Auth: console session cookie (log in once via POST /login).

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Purpose GET /api/v1/status live snapshot (stage, speed, queue, counters) GET /api/v1/jobs snapshot + last 25 runs POST /api/v1/jobs {"action": "start"\|"stop"} control the queue GET /api/v1/results all recovered credentials GET /api/v1/results.csv CSV export as JSON payload

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# login (cookie jar)
curl -c jar -d 'password=…' http://localhost:5000/login

# live status
curl -b jar http://localhost:5000/api/v1/status | jq

# start processing every uploaded capture
curl -b jar -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"action":"start"}' http://localhost:5000/api/v1/jobs

# poll results
curl -b jar http://localhost:5000/api/v1/results | jq '.results[].essid'

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text: Every command ships --help. Global behaviour comes from environment variables (WICRACK_* prefix) and data/web_state.json overrides.

docs.title: wicrack serve
docs.text: Flag Meaning --host / --port bind address (default 0.0.0.0:5000) --engine auto\|hashcat\|john force a backend --dry-run log planned commands without running them

docs.title: wicrack crack
docs.text:
Flag Meaning -f, --folder capture folder (default wifi_captures/) -y, --yes approve heavy stages without prompting --dry-run print the plan table and exit --no-benchmark skip the startup benchmark --engine force backend

Runs the full 12-stage pipeline per capture, stores results in SQLite, appends data/cracked_passwords.txt, exports CSV, and prints analytics.

docs.title: wicrack scan
docs.text: Convert captures and list every target (type, ESSID, BSSID) — useful to verify a capture actually contains handshakes before burning GPU time.

docs.title: wicrack bench
docs.text: Benchmark WPA (mode 22000) speed; cached for one hour in data/benchmark.json (--no-cache to force).

docs.title: wicrack report
docs.text:
wicrack report --format html --engagement "ACME Wireless Audit"
wicrack report --format evidence        # SHA-256 redacted by default

docs.title: wicrack assets download
docs.text: rockyou (~135 MB) and ortra (OneRuleToRuleThemAll.rule) from verified upstream URLs, with progress logging.

docs.title: wicrack vault export / read
docs.text: Fernet (AES + HMAC, PBKDF2 480k iterations) archive of every result. Losing the master password means losing the data — by design.

docs.title: wicrack selftest
docs.text: Six-point verification including a real end-to-end WPA crack (T5).

docs.title: Selection logic
docs.text:
wicrack inspects the machine once per run:

  1. --engine flag forces a backend, otherwise:
  2. hashcat available and reports > 0 OpenCL/CUDA GPU devices → hashcat
  3. else John the Ripper available → john (wpapsk, CPU SIMD)
  4. else hashcat on CPU (works, but slow for WPA)
  5. else: clear error with install instructions.

docs.title: hashcat backend
docs.text:
• mode 22000 (PMKID + EAPOL), -O optimized kernels, workload from settings
  • isolated potfile: data/potfile (no host potfile pollution)
  • live status parsing (Speed.#, Progress) → dashboard
  • optional hashcat brain client (auto-starts the server) to deduplicate candidates across workers
  • distributed splitting: --worker-id/--worker-total splits rules and wordlists (--skip/--limit) across machines

docs.title: John backend
docs.text:
• hash files converted with wpapcap2john (wpapsk format)
  • --rules=Best64 maps the best64 rule file to JtR's built-in section
  • mask mode uses JtR syntax (--mask, --1= custom charset) — verified against JtR docs, not copied from hashcat
  • combinator/hybrid kinds are skipped with a notice (JtR limitation); the CPU pipeline still covers straight/mask/stdin stages

docs.title: Adding a backend
docs.text: Implement wicrack.engines.base.Engine (four methods), return it from the selector, and every stage works automatically — that is the point of AttackSpec being declarative.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Component Purpose Install Python 3.10+ the framework itself distro package hashcat GPU cracking backend apt install hashcat hcxtools / hashcat-utils capture conversion apt install hcxtools hashcat-utils John the Ripper (jumbo) CPU backend (optional but recommended) apt install john tshark WPA3/SAE detection (optional) apt install tshark

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# from a clone
git clone https://github.com/ch-farhan107/WiCrackAgent.git
cd WiCrackAgent
bash install.sh --with-wordlists     # tools + rockyou + ORRTA rule

# or straight from pip (after the repo is published)
pip install wicrack
wicrack assets download --all        # wordlist + rule

docs.title: First run checklist
docs.text:
1. wicrack selftest — T5 proves an actual end-to-end WPA crack works.
  2. wicrack serve — the generated console password appears in the terminal; log in at http://localhost:5000 and change it in Settings.
  3. Upload a capture on the Upload tab, press START on Jobs.

docs.title: Getting a test capture (lab only)
docs.text: Assess your own AP in a lab: deauthenticate one of your clients with aircrack-ng's tooling, capture the re-handshake with airodump-ng -w lab, and drop the .cap into the console. Never capture third-party networks.

docs.title: Captures with spaces in the passphrase?
docs.text: That is stage C's whole job — plain tools miss those; WiCrackAgent generates append/prepend-space rules automatically.

docs.title: Heavy stages
docs.text: Big keyspaces (dive.rule, combinator) are estimated and gated: - CLI: interactive [y/N] prompt (or --yes) - Web: skipped unless Auto-approve heavy is enabled in Settings - Either: schedule with Heavy window (e.g. 22:00-06:00)

docs.title: Web console
docs.text: Start it with wicrack serve. The console binds to 0.0.0.0:5000 by default — keep it on a management network or an SSH tunnel, never the public internet.

docs.title: Tabs
docs.text: Tab Purpose Dashboard WebSocket live status: speed chart, current stage, queue, counters Upload drag-and-drop .cap/.pcap/.pcapng (size limit configurable) Settings wordlists, stage toggles, heavy window, notifications, filters, password Jobs START (queue every uploaded capture) / STOP (kill + cancel queue) Results cracked table + CSV / TXT / client HTML report downloads

docs.title: Live updates
docs.text: The dashboard opens a WebSocket (/ws) and receives a status snapshot every second. If WebSockets are unavailable (proxy, old browser) it degrades automatically to 3-second polling of /api/v1/status.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• On first run a random password is generated and printed to the terminal; it is stored (with the session secret) in data/web_state.json (mode 0600).
  • Change it under Settings → Security — persisted across restarts.
  • Sessions are HttpOnly cookies with SameSite=Lax.

docs.title: Console vs CLI behaviour
docs.text: Heavy stages need a decision the browser cannot make interactively. In web mode they are skipped unless Auto-approve heavy is on. Use the CLI when you want prompts.
